pairs.title: Operator domains, deficiency spaces and boundary realizations

A.title: Closed symmetric operators and deficiency data
A.statement: For a densely defined closed symmetric S on a complex Hilbert space define N±=ker(S*∓iE*) for a chosen reference energy E*>0; deficiency indices are dim N±. The graph core, adjoint domain and chosen boundary trace maps are part of the realization.
A.proof_route: Define kernels and prove their closedness using closedness of S*; explain E* nondimensionalization.

A.title: Unitary deficiency parameterization
A.statement: A closed densely defined symmetric S has a self-adjoint extension exactly when dim N+=dim N−. For each unitary U:N+→N− the extension has D(S_U)=D(S)⊕{u+Uu:u∈N+} and S_U(f+u+Uu)=Sf+iE*u−iE*Uu.
A.proof_route: Use the Cayley partial isometry, orthogonal range decompositions and graph-norm decomposition; check both adjoint inclusions, including infinite deficiency indices.

A.title: All interval Laplacian boundary conditions
A.statement: For L>0 the self-adjoint realizations of −d²/dx² between its minimal and maximal domains in L²(0,L) are parametrized by U∈U(2) through (U−I)Γ0f+iℓ(U+I)Γ1f=0, with Γ0=(f(0),f(L)), Γ1=(f′(0),−f′(L)) and fixed ℓ>0.
A.proof_route: Integrate by parts for boundary symplectic form, prove trace surjectivity with cubic polynomials, classify maximal isotropic planes by Cayley boundary coordinates.

A.title: A symmetric momentum with no self-adjoint extension
A.statement: The closure of −i d/dx initially on Cc∞(0,∞) has unequal deficiency indices (1,0), hence has no self-adjoint extension in L²(0,∞).
A.proof_route: Adjoint is maximal H¹; solve f′=∓f and test L² at infinity; use deficiency parameterization.

B.title: Twisted circle momentum
B.statement: For D(Pθ)={f∈H¹(0,L):f(L)=e^{iθ}f(0)}, Pθ=−iℏf′ has eigenvalues ℏ(2πn+θ)/L with normalized exponential eigenvectors.
B.proof_route: Fourier shift by e^{iθx/L} gives unitary equivalence to periodic Fourier multiplier.

B.title: Formal Hermiticity is insufficient
B.statement: The half-line derivative has a real formal differential expression after multiplying by −i but no self-adjoint extension; integration-by-parts symmetry alone does not produce unitary dynamics.
B.proof_route: Use the proved unequal deficiency indices.

pairs.title: Semibounded forms, variational spectra and Birman–Schwinger

A.title: Semibounded closed-form representation and perturbation
A.statement: A densely defined symmetric closed form q≥−c on a complex Hilbert space determines a unique self-adjoint H≥−c with Q(q)=D((H+c)^(1/2)) and q(u,v)=⟨Hu,v⟩ on D(H)×Q(q). If real v satisfies |v[u]|≤a q0[u]+b||u||² for q0≥0 and a<1, q0+v is closed and semibounded on Q(q0).
A.proof_route: Apply Riesz to q+(c+1)⟨.,.⟩ to construct bounded positive injective resolvent; invert on its range and use spectral calculus. Prove shifted form norm equivalence for perturbation.

A.title: Form min-max below the essential spectrum
A.statement: For semibounded self-adjoint H, λk=inf_dim L=k sup_||u||=1,u∈L qH[u], with L⊂Q(H), equals the kth eigenvalue below inf σess(H), counted with multiplicity, or that threshold if fewer exist. Compact form embedding gives a complete discrete eigenbasis.
A.proof_route: Prove spectral projection dimension bounds directly from the PVM; compact embedding gives compact shifted resolvent and use compact self-adjoint spectral theorem. Do not apply finite real Courant-Fischer to an unbounded complex operator.

A.title: Birman–Schwinger principle for bounded compact potentials
A.statement: For real W≥0 bounded and compactly supported on R³ and κ>0, Kκ=W^(1/2)(−Δ+κ²)^(−1)W^(1/2) is compact positive. The multiplicity of eigenvalue −κ² of −Δ−W equals that of 1 for Kκ; the number of eigenvalues below −κ² equals the number of eigenvalues of Kκ above 1.
A.proof_route: Kernel e^(−κ|x−y|)/(4π|x−y|) gives Hilbert-Schmidt compactness; intertwine eigenvectors, then compare negative form subspaces through (−Δ+κ²)^(1/2).

A.title: Rank-one resolvent and bound-state equation
A.statement: For self-adjoint H0, g∈H and real λ, let Hλ=H0+λ|g⟩⟨g|. With R0(z)=(H0−z)^(−1) and 1+λ⟨R0(z)g,g⟩≠0, Rλ=R0−λ R0|g⟩⟨g|R0/(1+λ⟨R0g,g⟩). Zeros below σ(H0) give bound states when g≠0.
A.proof_route: Multiply the proposed inverse on both sides on D(H0); use spectral measure derivative and monotonicity for eigenvalue count.

B.title: Separable attractive model
B.statement: For H0 multiplication by p² in L²(R³), g(p)=C exp(−p²/2) and λ<0, bound states solve 1+λ∫|g(p)|²/(p²+κ²)dp=0 and there is at most one.
B.proof_route: Derivative in κ has fixed sign; verify any threshold separately.

B.title: Trial states need the form domain
B.statement: A normalized L² vector outside Q(H) has no finite variational energy and supplies no Rayleigh–Ritz upper bound.
B.proof_route: Use free Fourier tail with finite L² norm and divergent weighted second moment.

pairs.title: Scattering channels, stationary resolvents and time delay

A.title: Wave, scattering and channel operators
A.statement: For self-adjoint H0,H on separable Hilbert spaces and bounded identification J, define Ω±=s-lim_t→±∞ e^(itH)J e^(−itH0)Pac(H0) where it exists; completeness means ran Ω±=Hac(H), and S=Ω+*Ω−. Two-space identifications and excluded bound sectors are explicit.
A.proof_route: Define the limit on a dense set then extend by uniform boundedness; distinguish completeness from isometry.

A.title: Compact-support short-range scattering closure
A.statement: For real bounded compactly supported V on R³, H=−Δ+V on H² has complete Ω± relative to −Δ, no singular continuous spectrum, and S is unitary on free L². Positive-energy stationary scattering agrees with the wave-operator scattering matrix with the retained normalization.
A.proof_route: Consume actual repaired compact-support completeness and stationary-dynamical identification carriers; prove compatibility of any changed Fourier convention and restrict all stationary claims to k>0.

A.title: Wigner–Smith matrix for differentiable finite channels
A.statement: If S(E)∈U(r) is C¹ on an energy interval, Q(E)=−iℏ S(E)*S′(E) is Hermitian, tr Q=−iℏ d log det S/dE, and under energy-independent unitary channel changes Q transforms by conjugacy.
A.proof_route: Differentiate S*S=I and determinant; an energy-dependent basis adds a connection term, which must be retained. This algebraic theorem does not prove an operational arrival-time interpretation.

A.title: Resonance poles in an analytic rank-one model
A.statement: If the scalar m(z)=⟨(H0−z)^−1g,g⟩ has a specified analytic continuation across an open absolutely continuous interval, noncancelled zeros of 1+λm_cont(z) give poles of the corresponding continued rank-one resolvent matrix elements. These poles are not complex eigenvalues of self-adjoint Hλ.
A.proof_route: Use the exact rank-one formula, state test-vector analytic continuation and nonzero numerator at the simple pole; derive residue. Existence of continuation is an explicit model input with Gaussian momentum form factor and an explicit contour.

B.title: Elastic phase derivative
B.statement: For S(E)=e^(2iδ(E)), Q(E)=2ℏδ′(E) has units seconds.
B.proof_route: Differentiate the phase; state differentiable branch and E away from thresholds.

B.title: Cook existence is not completeness
B.statement: An isometric intertwining wave operator need not have range all Hac(H); adding an uncoupled absolutely continuous summand to the target gives a counterexample.
B.proof_route: Take H=H0⊕H0 and Jf=(f,0).

pairs.title: Weyl quantization, Wigner functions and finite-time classical limits

A.title: Schwartz Weyl quantization and Wigner distributions
A.statement: For a∈S(R^(2d)) and ε>0 define OpεW(a)u(x)=(2πε)^−d∫e^(i(x−y)·ξ/ε)a((x+y)/2,ξ)u(y)dy dξ on Schwartz functions. For normalized u∈S define $W_\varepsilon[u](x,\xi)$=(2πε)^−d∫e^(−iy·ξ/ε)u(x+y/2)overline(u(x−y/2))dy.
A.proof_route: Absolute convergence, kernel Hilbert-Schmidt bound and Fourier inversion give well-definedness; extend the operator to L².

A.title: Wigner pairing and marginals
A.statement: For Schwartz symbols and states, ⟨OpεW(a)u,u⟩=∫a $W_\varepsilon[u]$; ∫$W_\varepsilon[u](x,\xi)$dξ=|u(x)|² and the position integral is the ε-Fourier momentum density. Wε is real but need not be nonnegative.
A.proof_route: Fubini and midpoint coordinate change; prove marginals using Schwartz Fourier inversion, not informal δ integration.

A.title: Weyl composition with a controlled Schwartz remainder
A.statement: For a,b∈S(R^(2d)) and 0<ε≤1, Op(a)Op(b)=Op(ab+(iε/2){a,b})+ε² Op(rε), with ||Op(rε)||≤C from finitely many fixed Schwartz seminorms of a,b. The Poisson bracket is ∂x a·∂ξ b−∂ξ a·∂x b.
A.proof_route: Derive the oscillatory product from two kernels, Taylor expand with integral remainder, integrate by parts until absolute convergence, and prove an L² kernel/Schur bound uniform in ε. Supply the full seminorm count in authoring.

A.title: Order-zero Weyl L² boundedness
A.statement: For each d there are a fixed integer Nd and Cd such that a∈C∞(R^(2d)) with bounded derivatives through Nd gives ||OpεW(a)||≤Cd∑_|α|≤Nd ||∂αa||∞, 0<ε≤1.
A.proof_route: Prove with phase-space cube partition, integration by parts and almost orthogonality; choose Nd=4d+4 as a sufficient nonoptimal index. This is a new local prerequisite, not an already accepted supplier.

A.title: Exact quadratic Egorov and finite-time smooth extension
A.statement: For a real quadratic h and its self-adjoint Weyl realization, Uε(t)*OpεW(a)Uε(t)=OpεW(a∘Φt), a Schwartz, where Uε=e^(−it Op(h)/ε) and Φt is the Hamiltonian flow. For h=|ξ|²/2+V(x), V smooth with all derivatives of order≥2 bounded, compact time intervals and compactly supported smooth a, an operator-norm O(ε²) remainder follows from an explicitly proved order-zero symbol estimate and cubic Moyal commutator remainder.
A.proof_route: Quadratic commutator is exact on S; integrate Heisenberg equation and extend boundedly. The nonquadratic branch requires a NEW local bounded-symbol lemma and cubic remainder, both specified in prose; it is not supplied by measure-theoretic Egorov.

B.title: Gaussian Wigner transport
B.statement: A Gaussian coherent state has positive Gaussian Wigner density with phase-space covariance saturating uncertainty; quadratic dynamics transports it exactly by the symplectic flow.
B.proof_route: Evaluate Gaussian Fourier integral and use quadratic Egorov.

B.title: Wigner negativity
B.statement: The first oscillator excited state has Wigner density proportional to (2(x²+ξ²)/ε−1)e^(−(x²+ξ²)/ε), which is negative near the origin.
B.proof_route: Evaluate Hermite Gaussian integral and normalize with the stated convention.

pairs.title: Projector geometry, adiabatic transport and Berry curvature

A.title: Smooth spectral bundles and Kato transport
A.statement: For a C² family of rank-r orthogonal projections P(x) on C^d over a smooth parameter manifold M, E={(x,v):P(x)v=v} has Hermitian fibers and projected connection ∇=P d. Along a C² path P(s), Kato transport solves W′=[P′,P]W, W(0)=I.
A.proof_route: Construct local frames by projecting a fixed independent r-tuple and Gram-Schmidt in a neighborhood; finite ODE gives unique transport.

A.title: Projector curvature and frame covariance
A.statement: For the projected connection of a C² rank-r projector family, F=P(dP∧dP)P. In a local orthonormal frame V with V*V=I, A=V*dV is anti-Hermitian and Fframe=dA+A∧A; under V→Vg, A→g^−1Ag+g^−1dg and F→g^−1Fg. Kato transport is unitary and P(s)W(s)=W(s)P(0).
A.proof_route: Differentiate P²=P to obtain PdPP=0; expand ∇² and use the local frame identity. Differentiate W*W and W*PW.

A.title: Rank-one holonomy and integral curvature
A.statement: For a C² rank-one projector on an oriented closed smooth surface, (i/2π)∫tr F is an integer equal to the first Chern number in this anti-Hermitian connection convention; local geometric phase is exp(−∮A), including transition functions when a path crosses frame patches.
A.proof_route: Use first Chern form agreement with topological line class; give two-chart clutching derivation using Stokes and winding, fixing orientation.

A.title: Physical adiabatic phase with explicit scale
A.statement: For C² finite Hermitian H(s) with a coherently followed spectral cluster separated by a uniform energy gap g>0, iℏ∂sUT=T H(s)UT transports the cluster up to leakage ≤ℏ C/T using X solving [H,X]=[P′,P]. For a simple eigenvalue, the comparison evolution factors into exp(−iT∫E ds/ℏ) and Kato geometric transport.
A.proof_route: Rescale the actual finite adiabatic supplier H→H/ℏ or T→T/ℏ; compute constants with energy units and use its intertwining evolution. Derive scalar phase by projecting the equation.

B.title: Spin-half curvature and a solid angle
B.statement: For P+=(I+n·σ)/2 on the unit sphere, a northern eigenframe gives A=i(1−cosθ)dφ/2 and F=i sinθ dθ∧dφ/2. Holonomy is exp(−iΩ/2) for the positive eigenline and oriented solid angle Ω modulo 4π.
B.proof_route: Differentiate normalized spinor (cos(θ/2),e^(iφ)sin(θ/2))ᵀ; integrate F with frame patch bookkeeping.

B.title: Slow variation alone is insufficient
B.statement: A path through a degeneracy may violate any uniform-gap adiabatic estimate; the constant cannot be held fixed as g→0.
B.proof_route: Use H(s)=s σz and a chosen branch whose labeling swaps at s=0; distinguish an actual discontinuous spectral choice from a coherently followed gapped projector.

pairs.title: Exchange symmetry, Schur–Weyl and Temperley–Lieb spin algebra

A.title: Unitary exchange blocks for collective spins
A.statement: On (C^d)^⊗N the permutation representation and diagonal U(d) action admit an orthogonal decomposition into Specht factors and multiplicity spaces indexed by partitions λ of N with at most d rows. Every permutation operator acts in the Specht factor; every collective U(d) action acts in the multiplicity factor.
A.proof_route: Start from exact published Schur-Weyl decomposition; choose invariant inner products by finite-group averaging and restrict GL(d) to U(d). Identify the finite commutants; no parastatistics assignment follows.

A.title: Singlet projectors form a Temperley–Lieb representation
A.statement: For N≥2 spin-half factors define si as adjacent swaps and ei=I−si=2Psinglet_(i,i+1). Then ei²=2ei, ei e_(i±1) ei=ei, and [ei,ej]=0 for |i−j|>1. This is a *-representation of TL_N(2), not a claim of faithfulness at all N.
A.proof_route: Check swap eigenvalues on singlet/triplet; compute contraction on three spinors using the normalized singlet. Tensor with identity to extend the local identity.

A.title: Exchange Hamiltonians in TL and spin blocks
A.statement: On a finite spin-half chain with dimensionless σ, Si=ℏσi/2 obeys Si·S_(i+1)=ℏ²(si/2−I/4)=ℏ²(I/4−ei/2). Therefore a finite exchange Hamiltonian ∑Ji Si·S_(i+1)/ℏ² is a Hermitian TL element commuting with global SU(2), with energies obtained independently in finite Schur-Weyl blocks.
A.proof_route: Use σaσb=δabI+iεabcσc and evaluate on singlet/triplet; retain Ji in joules and finite chain. The physical identification of exchange is an additional effective model.

A.title: Two-particle planar exchange and statistics holonomy
A.statement: The unordered configuration space of two distinct points in R² is homeomorphic to R²×(0,∞)×RP¹, hence its fundamental group is Z. Its one-dimensional unitary representations send the elementary exchange to e^(iθ), and a full winding to e^(2iθ). Bosonic/fermionic assignments θ=0,π are selected cases.
A.proof_route: Use center of mass, relative radius and relative angle modulo π; lift the angle to R and classify loops by winding. The flat line bundle is built from the universal cover quotient with that character.

B.title: Three spin-half decomposition
B.statement: Three spin-half factors decompose as one spin-3/2 multiplet and two spin-1/2 multiplets; nearest-neighbor exchange acts on the two-dimensional multiplicity space.
B.proof_route: Compute total spin highest weights and dimension 4+2+2=8; display the singlet-coupled basis and verify one exchange matrix.

B.title: Permutation invariance does not select statistics
B.statement: The identity Hamiltonian on a labeled tensor power commutes with all permutations while retaining every permutation sector. It does not force symmetric or antisymmetric physical states.
B.proof_route: Take N=2,d=2 and exhibit both singlet and triplet.

pairs.title: Regular Weyl systems, projective symmetry and massive particles

A.title: Finite canonical representation interface
A.statement: Assuming AC, a nonzero irreducible regular Weyl system on a finite-dimensional real symplectic space with fixed nonzero central parameter is unitarily equivalent to the Schrödinger system. Regularity, finite dimensionality and irreducibility are necessary hypotheses of this planning interface.
A.proof_route: Use actual current draft Stone–von Neumann carrier and its Mackey closure as draft planning suppliers; carry AC and do not infer infinite-mode uniqueness.

A.title: Mass cocycle for translations and boosts
A.statement: For m>0 on L²(R^d), T(a)f(x)=f(x−a) and B(v)f(x)=e^(imv·x/ℏ)f(x) satisfy B(v)T(a)=e^(imv·a/ℏ)T(a)B(v). Direct sums with distinct masses have distinct central characters.
A.proof_route: Multiply the two explicit unitary maps, prove strong continuity by dense smooth vectors, and identify the commutator scalar.

A.title: Spin rotations and projective SO(3)
A.statement: A spin-s irreducible unitary SU(2) representation has central element −I acting by (−1)^(2s); its ray action descends to SO(3). Half-integral spin gives a projective SO(3) action and integral spin an ordinary one.
A.proof_route: Use highest-weight spin basis and the 2π z-rotation eigenvalues e^(−2πim); show all m have the same parity.

A.title: Sector restriction as observable algebra
A.statement: For H=⊕_(j=1)^r Hj and allowed bounded observables A=⊕Aj, expectation tr(ρA) equals tr((∑PjρPj)A). Off-diagonal sector coherences are operationally invisible relative to that chosen algebra.
A.proof_route: Block multiplication and trace cyclicity; this is an algebra-relative theorem, not a proof that every mass coherence is forbidden.

B.title: Boost-translation loop phase
B.statement: The loop B(v)T(a)B(v)*T(a)* equals e^(imv·a/ℏ)I; relative phases can be observable only in an explicitly controlled path model.
B.proof_route: Use the cocycle and distinguish global phase on a single branch from relative phase.

B.title: Finite matrices cannot satisfy exact CCR
B.statement: No finite d×d matrices obey [Q,P]=iℏI with ℏ>0 because tr[Q,P]=0 but tr(iℏI)=iℏd.
B.proof_route: Take trace using cyclicity.

pairs.title: Measurement compatibility, dilation and identifiable tomography

A.title: Finite instrument dilation with an outcome register
A.statement: For finite completely positive maps Ia:M_d→M_e with ∑Ia trace preserving, there is an isometry V:C^d→C^e⊗C^q and mutually orthogonal register projections Qa with ∑Qa=I such that Ia(ρ)=TrE[(I⊗Qa)VρV*(I⊗Qa)].
A.proof_route: Apply existing Choi-Kraus theorem outcome by outcome, attach distinct |a,α⟩ basis vectors and check V*V=I. Do not duplicate the existing general instrument theorem.

A.title: Sharp finite joint measurability forces commutation
A.statement: Two finite PVMs {Pi},{Qj} admit a joint POVM {Gij} with marginals Pi,Qj exactly when every Pi commutes with every Qj; then Gij=PiQj.
A.proof_route: From 0≤Gij≤Pi derive Gij=PiGijPi by positive square root and kernel inclusion; sum over j and i to show PiQj=Gij.

A.title: Informationally complete linear tomography
A.statement: Input a finite POVM {Fa} spanning the real Hermitian d×d matrices and frequencies fa≥0 summing to one; compute Gram G_ab=tr(FaFb), its Moore-Penrose inverse, dual Da=∑b(G+)ab Fb and output X=∑a fa Da. X is Hermitian with exact reconstruction for model probabilities; positivity is not imposed.
A.proof_route: Define the finite spectral pseudoinverse and separate correctness from the procedure.

A.title: IID Bernoulli concentration
A.statement: For n independent Bernoulli(p) variables and f their average, P(|f−p|≥t)≤2 exp(−2nt²), t>0.
A.proof_route: Convexity bounds the centered one-variable log moment generating function by s²/8: its second derivative is a Bernoulli variance at most 1/4, and its value and derivative at zero vanish. Sum the bounds, use Markov, optimize s=4t, and apply both tails.

A.title: Tomography correctness and finite sample stability
A.statement: For the spanning POVM procedure, exact probabilities pa=tr(ρFa) recover ρ. A deterministic frequency error gives ||X−ρ||₂≤||D||_(ℓ²→HS)||f−p||₂. For n IID samples and m outcomes, with probability≥1−δ every |fa−pa|≤sqrt(log(2m/δ)/(2n)).
A.proof_route: Prove frame reconstruction by Gram pseudoinverse on its range; use Hoeffding for each indicator and union bound. IID and the true POVM are declared statistical assumptions.

B.title: Pauli six-outcome tomography
B.statement: The qubit POVM F_(j,±)=(I±σj)/6 is informationally complete and recovers ρ=(I+r·σ)/2 from differences rj=3(p_(j,+)−p_(j,−)).
B.proof_route: Use trace Pauli identities; finite frequencies may give |r|>1, illustrating lack of positivity.

B.title: Outcome probabilities do not fix disturbance
B.statement: The qubit Z PVM has both Lüders instruments and measure-then-prepare instruments with identical probabilities and different unconditional output states.
B.proof_route: Write Ia(ρ)=tr(Paρ)|+⟩⟨+| versus PaρPa; compare input |0⟩.

pairs.title: Finite reduced dynamics, memory and quantum trajectories

A.title: Finite system-environment and Markov model assignments
A.statement: A selected finite system and environment use a product initial state ρ⊗η and declared unitary U(t); reduced dynamics is Φt(ρ)=TrE U(t)(ρ⊗η)U(t)*. A time homogeneous GKSL model is a separately selected approximation with specified rates; it is not automatic from unitary reduction.
A.proof_route: Physical assignment and validity regime, not a proof of Markovianity.

A.title: Product-state reduced evolution is a channel
A.statement: Under the finite product-state environment model, each Φt is CPTP, but the family need not be a semigroup or CP-divisible.
A.proof_route: Diagonalize η=∑pk|k⟩⟨k| and use Kjk=√pk⟨j|U|k⟩; prove Kraus normalization. Give finite recurrent dephasing counterexample.

A.title: Amplitude damping with operational time units
A.statement: For an adopted qubit GKSL model H=ℏω|1⟩⟨1| and L=√γ|0⟩⟨1|, γ≥0 in s^−1, populations satisfy ρ11(t)=e^−γtρ11(0) and ρ01(t)=e^(iωt−γt/2)ρ01(0).
A.proof_route: Insert matrix units into the existing GKSL generator, solve linear ODEs and use published sufficient theorem for CPTP. No derivation from a vacuum continuum is claimed.

A.title: Finite jump expansion and ensemble equation
A.statement: For a finite GKSL generator with bounded jump operators, the no-jump contraction K(t)=exp[t(−iH/ℏ−∑L*aLa/2)] and time-ordered jump products define positive trajectory weights whose summed ensemble equals e^(tL)ρ. The expansion converges in trace norm on finite time intervals.
A.proof_route: Duhamel expansion of L=N+J, bound nth term by e^(t||N||)(t||J||)^n/n!, and trace-preserving total mass. This is an ensemble representation, not unique microscopic trajectories.

B.title: A finite bath revives coherence
B.statement: A system qubit coupled by H=ℏg σz⊗σz to an environment |+⟩ yields coherence multiplier cos(2gt); exact revivals contradict irreversible semigroup decay.
B.proof_route: Compute the two conditional environment phases and their overlap.

B.title: Single excitation jump law
B.statement: In the adopted amplitude damping model initially |1⟩, the first jump waiting-time survival is e^−γt and the state after the jump is |0⟩; no further jump occurs without a drive.
B.proof_route: Use K(t)|1⟩ and L|0⟩=0.

pairs.title: Finite-mode Fock, Gaussian and Bogoliubov foundations

A.title: Finite-mode quadratures and symplectic transformations
A.statement: For r≥1 use bosonic Fock over C^r, quadratures R=(Q1,P1,…,Qr,Pr) with [Rj,Rk]=iℏJjk on finite Hermite span. A Gaussian state is specified by characteristic function χ(z)=tr ρ exp(i z·R)=exp(i z·d−zᵀVz/2), with real d and real symmetric V; finite second moments are required.
A.proof_route: Use the existing closed ladder domains and oscillator ON basis; define exponentials by the regular Weyl system, not by an unbounded formal series.

A.title: Finite symplectic implementation by quadratic generators
A.statement: For each real S∈Sp(2r,R) there exists a unitary MS on L²(R^r) implementing MS* R MS=S R in the Weyl sense. Implementers are unique up to phase in the irreducible Schrödinger representation; the continuous double-cover choice is metaplectic.
A.proof_route: Decompose S into Fourier rotations, invertible coordinate changes and real quadratic chirps; prove each integral/unitary formula and its Weyl conjugation. Prove the decomposition with Gaussian elimination on Lagrangian blocks, including singular blocks. Use regular irreducibility for phase uniqueness.

A.title: Finite Bogoliubov implementability
A.statement: For finite r, matrices U,V with UU*−VV*=I and UVᵀ=VUᵀ define a′=Ua+Va† preserving CCR. There exists a unitary implementing this transformation on finite-mode Fock via the corresponding real symplectic matrix; mean number in the transformed vacuum is tr(VV*).
A.proof_route: Translate between complex ladder and real quadrature coordinates; apply explicit finite symplectic implementation and compute vacuum contraction. Unbounded equality holds on transported domains, while Weyl equality holds everywhere.

A.title: Positive definite Williamson normal form
A.statement: For real symmetric positive definite 2r×2r V there is S symplectic and positive νj such that V=S diag(ν1,ν1,…,νr,νr) Sᵀ. The uncertainty condition is equivalent to every νj≥ℏ/2.
A.proof_route: Diagonalize the real skew matrix V^(1/2)JV^(1/2) by an orthogonal matrix into νjJ2 blocks; rescale columns and check symplectic identities. Gaussian states satisfying uncertainty are positive definite in finite r, so no singular V branch is silently used.

A.title: Gaussian covariance and uncertainty
A.statement: For any state with finite quadrature second moments, V+iℏJ/2≥0. Under an implemented symplectic transformation, d→Sd and V→SVSᵀ. For finite-mode Gaussian χ, this inequality is also sufficient for existence of a density operator with that characteristic function.
A.proof_route: Necessity follows from ⟨C*C⟩≥0 for C=∑cj(Rj−dj); sufficiency requires the NEW Williamson diagonalization lemma below and product oscillator thermal states.

B.title: Single-mode squeeze statistics
B.statement: For a′=cosh(s)a+sinh(s)a†, s real, squeezed vacuum has mean number sinh²s and quadrature variances (ℏ/2)e^(±2s), with signs determined by the chosen implementer orientation.
B.proof_route: Substitute U,V, compute quadratures and verify determinant ℏ²/4.

B.title: Finite-mode implementability does not extend automatically
B.statement: For a formal infinite collection with identical nonzero squeezing s, the finite-N transformed vacuum has mean number N sinh²s and vacuum overlap (cosh s)^−N/2→0. The finite-dimensional theorem supplies no infinite-Fock implementer.
B.proof_route: Compute product expectations and overlap; do not use overlap alone as a full Shale–Stinespring proof.

pairs.title: Uniform magnetic fields, flux topology and Pauli coupling

A.title: Unbounded vector potential and Pauli model
A.statement: For m>0 and charge q, select the closed Friedrichs magnetic form qA[u]=(1/2m)∑||(-iℏ∂j−qAj)u||²+∫V|u|² on the closure of Cc∞ in its form norm, for smooth real A and real V∈L¹loc bounded below. A spin-half Pauli term −g q S·B/(2m) is an additional effective coupling with declared g and a semibounded realization.
A.proof_route: Separate physical minimal-coupling assignment from existence; form closure must be proved under the stated smooth/locally bounded hypotheses before use.

A.title: Exact planar Landau spectrum
A.statement: For constant nonzero B, q≠0, A=(0,Bx),V=0 on L²(R²), the Friedrichs magnetic Hamiltonian is unitarily equivalent to ∫⊕ h(k)dk with h(k)=−ℏ²∂x²/(2m)+(ℏk−qBx)²/(2m). Its spectrum is {ℏ|qB| (n+1/2)/m:n≥0}, each with infinite multiplicity and no continuous spectral measure.
A.proof_route: Partial Fourier transform in y followed by k-dependent x translation yields oscillator⊗I. Prove equivalence of forms and maximal coefficient domains; do not use bounded-A H² theorem.

A.title: Aharonov–Bohm ring holonomy
A.statement: A charge q constrained to a circle radius R with flux Φ uses HΦ=(ℏ²/(2mR²))(−i∂φ−α)² on periodic H², α=qΦ/(2πℏ). Its energies are ℏ²(n−α)²/(2mR²), n∈Z, and Φ→Φ+2πℏk/q is unitarily equivalent.
A.proof_route: Fourier diagonalization and gauge multiplication e^(ikφ); noninteger α cannot be removed by a single-valued periodic gauge.

A.title: Pauli square and g=2 model identity
A.statement: On Cc∞ spinors for smooth A, (σ·Π)²=Π²−qℏ σ·B with Π=−iℏ∇−qA. Therefore the quadratic Pauli Hamiltonian (σ·Π)²/(2m) gives g=2 at the formal-core level; its closed nonnegative form realization is selected separately.
A.proof_route: Use [Πi,Πj]=i qℏ εijk Bk and σiσj=δij+iεijkσk. Distinguish the model identity from a derivation of the electron anomalous magnetic moment.

B.title: Restoring longitudinal free motion
B.statement: The three-dimensional uniform-field Hamiltonian has bands En+ℏ²kz²/(2m) and absolutely continuous spectrum [ℏ|qB|/(2m),∞), unlike the planar Landau operator.
B.proof_route: Tensor planar spectral decomposition with the one-dimensional free momentum multiplier and integrate kz.

B.title: Half-flux degeneracy
B.statement: At α=1/2, ring states n=0 and n=1 are degenerate; at α=0 the ground state is unique.
B.proof_route: Compare the exact quadratic eigenvalue sequence.

pairs.title: Single-particle Bloch bundles and band topology

A.title: Lattice Bloch transform and band projectors
A.statement: For ℓ²(Z^d)⊗C^r and a finite-range translation-invariant Hermitian hopping operator (Hψ)n=∑δ Tδ ψ_(n−δ), T_(−δ)=Tδ*, define Fourier Bloch fibers h(k)=∑δ Tδ e^(−ik·δ), k∈T^d. An isolated group of bands defines the orthogonal spectral projector P(k).
A.proof_route: Fourier-series Parseval gives a unitary transform and bounded Hermitian matrix fibers; gap plus contour differentiation gives smooth P.

A.title: Gapped band curvature and Chern invariance
A.statement: For a C² gapped rank-r projector P(k) on the oriented two-torus, C=(i/2π)∫tr P dP∧dP is an integer, invariant under C² deformations preserving a uniform gap. A globally smooth periodic orthonormal frame forces C=0.
A.proof_route: Apply the projector curvature theorem to the determinant line bundle; prove the determinant transition connection and integrate exact transgression under homotopy.

A.title: Two-band Chern degree formula
A.statement: For smooth h(k)=d0(k)I+d(k)·σ with |d|>0 on T², the eigenprojectors P±=(I±n·σ)/2, n=d/|d|, satisfy C(P±)=∓(1/4π)∫n·(∂1n×∂2n)dk1dk2.
A.proof_route: Expand tr(P[∂1P,∂2P]) with Pauli matrices and the fixed i/(2π) convention. Prove integer degree by regular-value/chart winding or invoke the explicitly supplied line-class argument.

A.title: Conditional band velocity and anomalous term
A.statement: For a wave packet in a simple smooth isolated band and an explicitly adopted slow-force single-band approximation, the effective Lagrangian L=ℏk·xdot+ iℏ u(k)*∂k u(k)·kdot−E(k)+q Eext·x gives ℏkdot=qEext and xdot=(1/ℏ)∇kE−kdot×Ω, with Ω the real Berry curvature in the matching convention.
A.proof_route: Treat the Lagrangian as an effective model; perform Euler-Lagrange differentiation and match signs. Proving the wave-packet approximation error requires the semiclassical supplier and a new space-adiabatic theorem; this item claims only the conditional finite-dimensional variational consequence.

B.title: Lattice two-band gap locations
B.statement: For d=(sin kx,sin ky,M+cos kx+cos ky), the band gap closes precisely at M∈{−2,0,2}; on each complementary interval the Chern number is constant.
B.proof_route: Set all three components to zero and apply gap-preserving invariance; calculate integer values by degree with the stated orientation during authoring.

B.title: A nonzero Chern band has no global frame
B.statement: A band with nonzero C has no globally smooth periodic normalized eigenvector even though a smooth projector exists.
B.proof_route: Contradict vanishing of the integral of dA on a torus.

pairs.title: Periodic finite dynamics, quasienergy and controlled truncation

A.title: Finite Floquet unitary normal form
A.statement: For continuous T-periodic Hermitian H(t) on C^d, U(t)=P(t)e^(−itHF/ℏ) with a Hermitian HF and T-periodic unitary P(t). HF is defined from a chosen Hermitian logarithm of U(T), and quasienergies are defined modulo 2πℏ/T.
A.proof_route: Diagonalize U(T), select eigenphases and set HF; define P(t)=U(t)e^(itHF/ℏ), use periodic propagator composition.

A.title: Finite-level Sambe operator with Fourier domain
A.statement: For C¹ periodic finite Hermitian H(t), K=H(t)−iℏ∂t on L²(S¹_T)⊗C^d with periodic H¹ domain is self-adjoint as a bounded perturbation of the Fourier derivative. Its eigenvectors e^(inωt)P(t)vj have eigenvalues εj+nℏω.
A.proof_route: Use the explicit periodic derivative multiplier, Kato–Rellich and the Floquet normal form; verify the conjugating periodic unitary preserves H¹.

A.title: Finite model truncation with bounded coupling error
A.statement: For finite Hermitian H and projection P, let HD=PHP+(I−P)H(I−P), V=H−HD. Then ||e^(−itH/ℏ)−e^(−itHD/ℏ)||≤|t| ||V||/ℏ. Consequently leakage from ran P is bounded by this number.
A.proof_route: Differentiate e^(−i(t−s)H/ℏ)e^(−isHD/ℏ), integrate and use unitarity. No unbounded coupling estimate follows without domain control.

A.title: Floquet Fourier–Galerkin assembly
A.statement: Input d, Fourier coefficients Hm with H_(−m)=Hm*, finite harmonic bandwidth b, ω>0 and cutoff N≥0; output the Hermitian matrix K_nm=H_(n−m)+nℏω δnm I for −N≤n,m≤N. Assemble blocks and diagonalize to requested numerical tolerance with a declared classical eigensolver.
A.proof_route: Finite loops terminate after (2N+1)² block assignments; correctness means exact compression of the Sambe operator, not automatic convergence of all computed quasienergies.

A.title: Fourier–Galerkin assembly correctness and termination
A.statement: The specified Fourier–Galerkin assembly terminates after finitely many block operations and its exact output matrix is the orthogonal compression of K to harmonics −N,…,N; it is Hermitian. Numerical diagonalization accuracy is a separate residual claim.
A.proof_route: Compute each Fourier matrix element of multiplication and derivative, use H_(−m)=Hm*, and count a finite square index set.

B.title: Commuting longitudinal drive
B.statement: For H(t)=(E0+A cosωt)σz, U(t)=exp[−i(E0t+(A/ω)sinωt)σz/ℏ]; one Floquet choice is HF=E0σz and P(t)=exp[−iA sinωt σz/(ℏω)].
B.proof_route: Integrate the commuting family and verify periodicity.

B.title: Quasienergy has no canonical ground state
B.statement: Changing the logarithm eigenphase by 2π changes a quasienergy by ℏω without altering the monodromy. A lowest quasienergy is therefore not invariant without a selected branch.
B.proof_route: Use a one-level time-independent Hamiltonian and add nℏω.

pairs.title: Variational approximation, residual certificates and propagation errors

A.title: Conforming Rayleigh–Ritz procedure
A.statement: Input a semibounded closed form q, finite independent vectors φj∈Q(q), Gram matrix Gij=⟨φj,φi⟩ and form matrix Aij=q(φj,φi). Output eigenvalues and G-normalized coefficients of Ac=λGc after positive Gram factorization.
A.proof_route: Define exact arithmetic procedure and required quadrature enclosure if entries are numerical; no hidden assumption that trial vectors lie in D(H).

A.title: Conforming Ritz eigenvalue upper bounds
A.statement: Each kth Rayleigh–Ritz value from an n-dimensional conforming form subspace is ≥ the kth min-max spectral value for k≤n, and nested dense form subspaces converge to every isolated eigenvalue below essential spectrum.
A.proof_route: Restrict the min-max infimum and approximate a finite spectral eigenspace in the form norm; control its Gram matrix and energy uniformly.

A.title: Residual distance and isolated-eigenspace certificate
A.statement: For self-adjoint H, normalized u∈D(H), real λ and r=(H−λ)u, dist(λ,σ(H))≤||r||. If all spectrum outside a selected cluster lies at distance≥g>0 from λ, then ||(I−Pcluster)u||≤||r||/g.
A.proof_route: Integrate |x−λ|² against the scalar PVM; a spectral gap lower-bounds the integral off the cluster. A nearby spectral point need not be the intended eigenvalue without counting/gap information.

A.title: A posteriori Schrödinger propagation bound
A.statement: Let H be self-adjoint, v(t) a C¹ H-valued path with v(t)∈D(H), Hv continuous and r=iℏv′−Hv integrable. Then ||v(t)−e^(−itH/ℏ)v(0)||≤ℏ^−1∫0^|t| ||r(s)||ds with the corresponding oriented interval.
A.proof_route: Differentiate the interaction-picture vector using the stated graph regularity, integrate the residual and apply unitarity.

B.title: Hermite Ritz exactness
B.statement: For the oscillator, the span of the first n true Hermite states yields exactly its first n eigenvalues and zero residuals.
B.proof_route: Use the already authored coefficient-domain oscillator theorem.

B.title: A small residual does not label an eigenvalue
B.statement: For H=diag(0,100), vector (0,1) has zero residual at λ=100 although it is not a ground-state approximation.
B.proof_route: Compute directly; distinguish inclusion from eigenvalue indexing.

pairs.title: Finite-mode light–matter models and detection statistics

A.title: Finite-mode dipole and detector assignment
A.statement: Select finitely many oscillator modes, a finite atomic Hilbert space and compressed dipole matrices. Specify mode frequencies, coupling constants and photon-count/homodyne POVMs. Long-wavelength, rotating-wave and Markov approximations are separate optional assumptions with named scale regimes.
A.proof_route: State units and physical calibration; the finite-mode model does not establish exact electromagnetic localization or continuum photon spin.

A.title: Jaynes–Cummings invariant blocks and Rabi frequency
A.statement: Under the rotating-wave two-level single-mode assignment H=ℏω a†a+(ℏω0/2)σz+ℏg(aσ++a†σ−), real g, the excitation N=a†a+σ+σ− is conserved on finite-particle core. Each span{|e,n⟩,|g,n+1⟩} has splitting ℏsqrt(Δ²+4g²(n+1)), Δ=ω0−ω. The orthogonal block direct sum defines a self-adjoint Hamiltonian on its squared-block-norm domain.
A.proof_route: Compute the two-by-two blocks and commutator on core; define self-adjointness by direct sum of finite Hermitian matrices, not bounded-perturbation of a†a without proof.

A.title: Passive beam-splitter photon statistics
A.statement: For a passive two-mode unitary with a1→t a1+r a2, |t|²+|r|²=1 and the full two-by-two matrix unitary, input |n,0⟩ gives output counts Binomial(n,|t|²). Coherent input |α,0⟩ gives a product of coherent outputs with amplitudes determined by that unitary.
A.proof_route: Transform creation polynomials and normalize using factorial ladder norms; use finite-mode implementation and exponential coherent expansion.

A.title: Pure loss channel and binomial thinning
A.statement: Mix a single mode with an independent vacuum mode by a passive beam splitter and trace the latter. The resulting CPTP map sends number n to binomial photon statistics and coherent α to coherent sqrt(η)α, 0≤η≤1.
A.proof_route: Use the actual isometric dilation on infinite-dimensional finite-mode Fock; prove trace-norm definition by positive trace-class approximation and partial trace, not finite-dimensional Choi classification.

B.title: Vacuum Rabi oscillation
B.statement: On resonance and initial |e,0⟩, excitation probability equals cos²(gt) in the ideal Jaynes–Cummings model; it revives and is not irreversible spontaneous decay.
B.proof_route: Exponentiate the n=0 block.

B.title: Ideal single-mode factorial moment
B.statement: For number state |1⟩ and ideal number measurement, ⟨a†a†aa⟩=0 while ⟨a†a⟩=1, so g²(0)=0 in that single-mode normally ordered detector model.
B.proof_route: Evaluate ladder action; separate model prediction from an actual reported experiment and from multimode detection.
